definitions.absent: Effectively absent from the normal character experience.
definitions.available: A genuine secondary or situational option, but not a defining strength.
definitions.core: A strong, regularly useful and identity-defining part of the character experience.

scoringRules: Score the expected play experience across a normal Pathfinder 1e campaign, not a single optimised build.
A capability may support more than one criterion when it genuinely answers different player intentions.
Do not reward raw power, action-economy efficiency or system tier unless the criterion explicitly measures the resulting play experience.
A class receives a complete profile. An archetype inherits it and stores only material overrides.
Capability levels describe the candidate. Preference importance from 1 to 10 and Not relevant are separate request fields.
Multiple capabilities may be core simultaneously; the scale is not a forced either-or axis.

criteria.definition: Reliably contributing through weapons, natural attacks or unarmed combat at close range.
criteria.boundary: Do not award for durability alone or for merely being able to carry a weapon.

criteria.definition: Reliably contributing through bows, crossbows, firearms, thrown weapons or other non-spell ranged attacks.
criteria.boundary: Spell attacks belong under Offensive Magic unless a weapon attack remains the primary delivery method.

criteria.definition: Using spells or supernatural powers as a regular means of directly harming enemies.
criteria.boundary: Pure conditions without meaningful direct harm belong under Debuffing Enemies.

criteria.definition: Concentrating meaningful damage on one priority target.
criteria.boundary: Score the outcome regardless of whether it comes from weapons, spells or companions.

criteria.definition: Damaging several enemies in an area or through reliable multi-target attacks.
criteria.boundary: Do not award for control effects that cause no meaningful damage.

criteria.definition: Using trips, grapples, disarms, bull rushes, feints or comparable physical techniques.
criteria.boundary: Terrain, magical zones and broad action denial belong under Battlefield Control.

criteria.definition: Directing allies through commands, teamwork benefits, granted movement or coordinated positioning.
criteria.boundary: Generic numerical buffs without a leadership or coordination component belong under Support and Buffing.

criteria.definition: Surviving through hit points, armour, avoidance, resistances, mitigation or self-defence.
criteria.boundary: Protecting other characters is scored separately.

criteria.definition: Intercepting attacks, absorbing or redirecting harm, defending positions or preventing enemies reaching allies.
criteria.boundary: Magical wards may also support Defensive and Protective Magic when magic is central to the protection.

criteria.definition: Restricting movement or actions through terrain, zones, walls, forced positioning or broad crowd control.
criteria.boundary: Single-target penalties belong primarily under Debuffing; direct physical manoeuvres have their own criterion.

criteria.definition: Repositioning, charging, flying, teleporting or fighting effectively while mounted or on the move.
criteria.boundary: A mount increases this score only when it materially improves normal combat movement.

criteria.definition: Imposing penalties, conditions, fear, curses or other disadvantages on enemies.
criteria.boundary: A spell can score here and in Offensive Magic only when it both harms and meaningfully debilitates.

criteria.definition: Dispelling, countering, interrupting, suppressing or resisting hostile magic and comparable special abilities.
criteria.boundary: General saving throws or passive toughness alone are Personal Durability.

criteria.definition: Improving allies' attacks, defences, movement, skills or other capabilities.
criteria.boundary: Direct coordination and command mechanics may additionally support Tactical Leadership.

criteria.definition: Restoring hit points, removing harmful conditions or returning allies to effective action.
criteria.boundary: Temporary prevention of harm belongs under protection rather than recovery.

criteria.definition: Creating magical wards, barriers, resistances, immunities or other preventative protections.
criteria.boundary: This measures magical protection specifically; mundane guarding belongs under Protecting Allies.

criteria.definition: Using magic for travel, detection, communication, exploration and non-damage problem solving.
criteria.boundary: Knowledge gained through skills rather than magic belongs under Knowledge and Investigation.

criteria.playerLabel: Adventuring with summoned or bonded allies
criteria.definition: Relying on summoned creatures, familiars, animal companions, mounts, eidolons or comparable entities.
criteria.boundary: Score centrality and usefulness, not the mere presence of a cosmetic companion.

criteria.definition: Changing shape, adopting aspects, mutating or substantially altering the character's body and capabilities.
criteria.boundary: Simple numerical self-buffs without a transformation fantasy do not qualify strongly.

criteria.definition: Solving practical problems through skills such as traps, devices, crafting, medicine, navigation or specialised tools.
criteria.boundary: Knowledge skills and wilderness identity are scored separately; profession identity is categorical.

criteria.definition: Persuading, deceiving, intimidating, entertaining, leading or navigating social situations.
criteria.boundary: A high Charisma score alone is insufficient without meaningful class support or expected use.

criteria.definition: Applying lore, research, perception of clues, divination or investigative methods.
criteria.boundary: Hands-on technical solutions belong under Practical Expertise.

criteria.definition: Infiltrating, hiding, disguising, deceiving tactically or striking from concealed advantage.
criteria.boundary: Social deception without infiltration belongs primarily under Social Influence.

criteria.definition: Tracking, surviving, navigating nature, handling animals and mastering wild environments.
criteria.boundary: A single class skill is insufficient; the wilderness must be a supported part of the play experience.
